utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, will you have the accused brought in, and also give us the case number, since we're starting on a new legal foundation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is case number IT-95-10-T.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me wait for the accused to be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like representations for the parties. First for the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Nice, would you please tell us who is with you? That is yourself, of course, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Tochilovsky.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I see you have an assistant with you. Perhaps you could introduce her to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Ms. Reynders, the case manager, has been with us throughout, and indeed she's here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Turning to the Defence, please, would you identify yourselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Jelisic, along with my colleague, Mr. Greaves. My name is Mr. Londrovic, and we have an interpreter with us from the secretariat, Mrs. Meliha Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I want to say for the public gallery that we are now beginning the sentencing hearings, after which a sentence will be issued by this Trial Chamber for Mr. Jelisic, who is sitting to my right, who, as each person knows, has pleaded guilty to crimes against humanity and war crimes. I think that without any further adieu, I can turn to Mr. Greaves or Mr. Londrovic so that they can tell us how the Defence is going to organise its work, since you must take the initiative, and you can now tell us how things are going to be organised. In respect of the various orders that we issued, we set up a framework, that is, a time frame, and that there will also be video conference hearings. I would like to recall, for the sake of the public, that this is going to be held in public except when the witness is brought into the courtroom, because he is protected. After that, we will raise the blinds. Mr. Greaves, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I'm going to call witnesses who are present in The Hague, who are going to be called into the courtroom this afternoon. Tomorrow morning, as Your Honour knows, there is a period when we're going to deal with some videolink witnesses. That, I hope, we shall complete, subject to the technical problems that may arise, in the morning, and then in the afternoon we shall continue with live witnesses. I understand that on Wednesday, there will be a further session of two witnesses to be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no transcript emerging on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I draw Your Honour's attention to the fact that we have no transcript coming through on our computers on the Defence side. THE COURT REPORTER: It will just be a moment, Sir, or possibly a few more minutes, but it will all come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. Without delaying matters any further, I would ask Witness DJ to come into the court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you hear me, Witness? First of all, do you hear me in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're going to nod to tell us whether the name on the piece of paper we're showing you is yours. Make sure it is you. Don't say your name. Simply say that it is you. All right. Very well. Now you're going to take an oath. Please remain standing for a few more moments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may now be seated. Witness DJ -- that's what we're going to call you -- you are being covered by protective measures, very strict ones, measures that were asked for by the Defence, and you have come to testify during the sentencing hearings being conducted against Mr. Jelisic, who is in this courtroom to your left. First of all, you're going to be asked questions by Defence counsel, Mr. Greaves, and then questions will be put to you by the Prosecution. Mr. Greaves, you may proceed. We can raise the blinds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DJ, can you tell Their Honours, please, what is your ethnic background, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, when it was that you first, during the course of your life, got to know Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I have known Goran for many years, from elementary school and secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you first got to know him, was that as a friend or as an acquaintance with whom you would exchange greetings but perhaps no more than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: A little more than an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you could describe yourself as a friend of Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And at what age were you when you became his friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were you still at school or had you left school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I was still at school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And the group of friends of which you were one, what was the ethnic mix of that? Was it exclusively Muslim, or exclusively Serb, or how would you describe his group of friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Most of them were Muslims, but it was a mixed group.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did your friendship continue with Goran Jelisic up until the war that broke out in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And prior to the war breaking out, did you ever hear Goran Jelisic expressing anti-Muslim views, extremist views that expressed hate towards Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If he had done so, could you have remained his friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I cannot believe that he did that, and he's a friend for life, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Upon the outbreak of fighting in your hometown, Witness DJ, can you tell us, first of all, what the date when that fighting broke out was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: On the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And when the fighting broke out, did you take any part in military operations of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I felt the need to defend my town, and I was up at the barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And were those barricades that were set up by organised military forces or by ad hoc groups of civilians? How were they set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: A group of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And the people on those barricades, were they in possession of firearms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long did you remain on the barricades for, Witness DJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Three to four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And at the end of that three to four days, did you retain your weapon, or what happened to the weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: The Serbs asked us to hand over our weapons, and we did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In the week after the weapons had been handed over, were there any problems for you personally because of what you had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What was the nature of those problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I was mistreated, taken in. And people were even killed, those who had taken part at the barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As a result of what you became aware of, did you have any fears for your personal safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What did you think might happen to you because of your activities on the barricades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Probably murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Without telling us any names, Witness DJ, apart from yourself, were there other members of your immediate family living in your hometown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you discuss with them what you should do as a result of your fears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Having discussed it with them, what was the conclusion to which you came, what was the decision to which you came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: That I had to flee (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And as a result of taking that decision, did you discuss with anybody outside your family what you should do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, with a friend of mine, and I don't wish to state his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I don't want to ask you his name. Was he a Muslim, or a Serb, or what ethnic group was he from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And did that person give you any help to flee the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No. Quite the contrary. He refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: He refused. The person to whom you turned, was he a very close friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How did you feel, that your close friend had let you down in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, I felt terrible. Well, I felt terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: At this time, were you taking any measures to keep out of the way of possible trouble?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What were you doing to avoid trouble, Witness DJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: When I saw the police, I fled and took refuge with my father-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can you remember, how long after the ending of the barricades did the police officers come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: About seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you give any instructions as to what should be told to the police if they came to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I told my father and my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What did you tell to your father and family to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I told them to say that they didn't know where I was and that I hadn't been home for several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you reach the home of your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you got to the home of your father-in-law, what part of the house did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: The basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Whilst you were in the basement, did a member of your family come to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Are you married, Witness DJ? Don't tell us, if you are, what your wife's name is, but are you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When did you next see your wife after you had fled your home and gone to hide in the cellar of your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: After I had come back from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves, I don't want the witness to have to tell us his entire life. Don't forget that these are presentencing hearings. I think that you're trying to demonstrate mitigating circumstances, but I would like for the discussion to be focused. I would like to take the liberty of reminding you of that. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DJ, when you next saw your wife, did she tell you of any conversation that she had had with anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: With whom did your wife tell you she had spoken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: With Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did she tell you how the conversation had come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what was the nature of the conversation she had had with Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: My wife met Goran Jelisic in town. Goran asked her how I was, and she said that I was having problems and that I needed help.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As a result of that conversation, did you get in touch with Goran Jelisic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you telephoned him -- did you meet him, or telephone him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He came to my father-in-law's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And when he came to your father-in-law's house, did you tell him what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As a result of telling him what had happened to you, what did Goran Jelisic do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He offered to take us, and he said that we would be safe with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you accept that offer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I thought about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long did you think about it for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. Two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And having thought about it, did you decide to take up the offer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, we did, because there was no other way out for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And as a result of that, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: We went to Goran's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: First of all, how long in all did you spend at Goran's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Seven days, seven to eight days, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And during the time you were at Goran's house, did you see much of Goran himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did. To my surprise, I was exceptionally satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And just to make it clear, was he aware that you were being sought by the police for having been on the barricades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Apart from Goran Jelisic, were other members of his family in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, his father, his mother, and his sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: During the time you were at Goran Jelisic's house, did you become aware of information concerning other members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And without, again, telling us any names, but did you hear it from a friend, or from a particular relation of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: From my father-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And again, without telling us names, was what the nature of the information about members of your family that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: My friend in the meantime had gone to (redacted) (redacted), to his wife's place, and he was taken prisoner there with his child, and they forced him to have me surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you in fact surrender, or did you think about surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, I thought about surrendering, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you discuss that with Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I did, and he told me not to surrender but to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he give you a reason why he thought you should wait?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Because my brother and his child had done nothing wrong and that they would have to release them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you accept that advice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were those people eventually released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, they were, because the inhabitants of (redacted) went to help my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with Goran Jelisic about any further plans for leaving the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What did Goran Jelisic tell you about those plans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He said he would help me and do everything in his power to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As a result of these discussions, did you go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: To Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you go to Brcko by a direct route, or did you have to go by an indirect route?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, half the time I used the indirect road and the other half the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason why you had to go on an indirect route?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what was that reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, had we been stopped by the police, I think that they would have killed Goran and me together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And why was Goran Jelisic at risk of being killed in these circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, probably because he had a good heart and was a good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you got to Brcko, did you go somewhere in particular in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, Goran went to a friend, and I don't know his name to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And were arrangements made for you to leave Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. This man promised that he would take us off to Gunja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you have a discussion of any kind with Goran Jelisic about recompensing him in any way for the efforts that he'd made for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I offered him money, but he emphatically refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: While you were awaiting your opportunity to leave Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you able to make any arrangements for anybody else to leave with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Again, don't give us any names, but were they members of your family, or were they friends, or what relation did they stand to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: They were members of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Having made those arrangements, did those members of the family come to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In due course, did you manage to cross into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And apart from you, was that all the members of your family for whom arrangements had been made? Did they go at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And can you remember the date upon which you left Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: The 20th of April, we crossed to Gunja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In due course, did you become a refugee outside the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you remain in contact with Goran Jelisic once you had become a refugee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you contact him by phone, or by letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: By phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you have any further discussion with him on any of those occasions about recompense for what he had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And again, what was his reaction on that occasion to the suggestion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He didn't even want to hear about it, and he said that I would have helped him had he been in that kind of situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that some members of your family were able to leave in April 1992, but did any members of your family remain behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, my sister and my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you remain in contact with your sister and father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was that by telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, but using a neighbour's phone, because we didn't have one in our own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were you able to speak to your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, but only the basic sort of conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you learn if Goran Jelisic had paid any visits or made any contact with your sister or your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions, Goran went to visit my father and sister. He would bring them cigarettes and coffee and sugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: From your sister and from your father, did you become aware of a change in the population of Bijelina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What was the nature of the change of population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: There was a great influx of refugees, and they had to leave their town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And were those refugees, were they Muslim, or were they Serb refugees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did your sister and your father experience any problems as a result of the influx of these refugees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What was the nature of those problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: They came and threatened them, mistreated them, to make them leave their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As a result of hearing about that, did you contact Goran Jelisic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As a result of that contact, were any arrangements made in respect of your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: At that time, how old was your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He was 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And was he in good health at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In due course, did your father succeed in leaving Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What about your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And did they in fact leave the former Yugoslavia completely and come and live with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And from them, did you learn how it was they had managed to leave Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, thanks to Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And how was it that Goran Jelisic had managed to effect their escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Goran is a passionate fisherman, and he took them across the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he help any other members of your family at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. He helped my uncle and aunt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How did he help them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He took them, together with my father and sister, to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And in which year did this all take place, Witness DJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: This was in '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Is it within your knowledge as to whether helping people of Muslim ethnicity at that time still presented a risk to the life of Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, it did. It exposed them to great danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you know if any money was offered to Goran Jelisic to carry out the escape of your father and sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. I offered money to him. Goran emphatically declined, and he never took a single penny from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think your father died eventually in 1997, Witness DJ. Did he have anything to say on the subject of Goran Jelisic before he died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. He requested that we never forget Goran, because if it weren't for him, maybe half of my family wouldn't be alive today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And by that time, were you and your family, as a whole, aware that accusations had been levelled against him in respect of serious crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I couldn't believe, and I, to this day, still don't believe that this man could have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DJ, he's pleaded guilty before the Tribunal to committing a number of murders and other offences, and the victims were, in fact, Muslims. Does that knowledge in any way change your opinion of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No. He is a friend to me, and he will remain my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DJ, will you please wait there and answer any questions which may be asked of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Greaves. I would like to congratulate you for having been so concise and having gone directly to the core of the testimony that you wanted to bring out. Mr. Nice, you now ask the questions. Witness DJ, you're going to answer the Prosecutor's questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The incidents in Bijeljina occurred in which month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Everything of which you have spoken concerning your own escape occurred before the bridges were blown in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: The bridge in Brcko, in Gunja, was half destroyed by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There was still access between Brcko and Croatia at the time of your escape, for there was still part of the bridge left standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before the incidents in Bijeljina, you were aware of Goran Jelisic's criminal activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I was not aware of criminal activities of Goran Jelisic. I knew him, but we were not best friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You knew nothing of his going to court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Something -- a little bit, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You knew nothing of the sentence of imprisonment imposed on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And he never mentioned that to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I frequently went out -- went to Germany and Austria, so perhaps that happened at the time while I was abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What were you doing in Germany and Austria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: In Germany, I worked in Baustelle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Building construction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I see. How much of your time were you spending in Germany and Austria before the incidents at Bijeljina? Most of your time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Not a majority of time. I would go there for about two or three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Coming up to date, are you still living in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You say that you moved from Bijeljina to Brcko sometimes on a main road, sometimes elsewhere. Are you saying that Jelisic was with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What date was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I think it was the 19th, because there was this huge panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The 19th was the day that you, what, left Bijeljina, the 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The journey along the road, did that involve passing checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No. Goran went around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So at that stage, Goran Jelisic had enough information to know how to get around the checkpoints, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I don't know if he had sufficient information, but he did know those indirect roads well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He had more knowledge than you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he got that knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, we all know Bijeljina and its surroundings. I never asked him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he tell you whether he was already involved with the Serbian authorities at that stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No. At that moment when he was helping me, he was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So you discovered that he was involved with the authorities at a later stage, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I heard something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What did he tell you about his getting involved with the Serbian authorities? Did he tell you about it on this trip through to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Goran did not go with me to Croatia, only as far as Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In Brcko, how long did he stay with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: A short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Days, hours, weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Maybe an hour, hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And he, what, had contacts in Brcko at that stage to help you move on to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, he did, but it was just a plain man.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You say "just a plain man." We may not want to identify the man, but did the man have some particular power or authority that he was able to get you out of Brcko and into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No, he wasn't highly placed. He was just an ordinary man who lived in that city, and he knew the crossing to Gunja.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The crossing to Gunja, just help us, is that across the bridge that was still standing or is that another way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Across the bridge. The bridge was half destroyed, and then the rest was something that was just made up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So that Jelisic stayed with you for a time, handed you over to his friend, and then where did Jelisic go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: He went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Along the same dangerous road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know which roads he took.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He hadn't, by now, told you anything of his contact with Serbian authorities. When did you learn about those contacts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: From newspapers and television.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How much later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: A fair amount later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of course, by the time in 1993 when you tell us that other members of your family were assisted, Jelisic was known to be a wanted man, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He was known to have been suspected of committing these crimes in Brcko, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Maybe you were aware of that, but I was busy working all day, so I simply wasn't interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The area you live in now, is it a Serb area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: The city used to be a Muslim -- mostly inhabited by Muslims, but the surrounding towns were mostly inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And at present, they are mostly inhabited by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Are those Serb authorities aware that you're here today? Just "yes" or "no".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We only have your name, which mustn't be given publicly; we have no other details of you. Are you content to provide the Prosecution with your date of birth -- you don't have to, and if you do, it can be provided on a piece of paper -- or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, for my own security, I would rather not do it. But if it is a requirement, then no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The word "balija" uttered against a Muslim would be extremely offensive, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Depends for whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: For the Muslim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I am from a mixed marriage, I'm only half Muslim, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The other half of your ethnic background being what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: My wife is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I repeat. Using the word "balija," especially in an abusive way against Muslims, would be highly offensive, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Muslims being forced or compelled to sing Serbian songs would be a highly-offensive thing to do, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Nice. Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to deal with one matter in private session, please, if I may.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness DJ, you were asked by counsel for the Prosecution about when it was you learnt that Goran Jelisic had been involved in any way with the Serbian authorities, and I think the answer that you gave was that it was much later. Can you be any more specific as to when the first time you learnt of his participation in any -- or allegations of his participation in any sort of criminal -- crimes of violence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an exact date. I learned things from the newspapers, and that's really all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was that after the escape of your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I have no further questions in re-examination. Do Your Honours have any questions for the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll ask the question -- Judge Riad, did you have a question? First Judge Riad is going to ask some questions that he wants to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness DJ, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I understood from your answers that Mr. Jelisic saved half of your family in the way you described, after saving you, of course, and in the meantime, in one of your answers to the Prosecutor, you said that you knew him but you were not best friends. What made Mr. Jelisic so keen on saving you and your family, and what made you so confident to accept his help, and you knew that you might be trapped, it could be a trap? You were very confident in his help, and apparently he did save your -- half of your family. And you were not best friends, so I feel some kind of missing link here. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Let me answer you. I know Goran Jelisic. We frequently sat in cafes, talked about sports and about girls. We never talked about ethnic issues. I did not really have a choice. Goran was the only one who offered to help me. There was, of course, a possibility that that would be a trap, but that could also be a salvation, and I had no choice, so I had to accept it. And in the end, it ended well, and I'm very grateful to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Perhaps you can help me, then, understand more. You said, of course, you don't know if he helped other people, too. Did he help other people, other Muslims around you, to your knowledge? Was it some kind of generous attitude towards the Muslims, helping whom he can, even though they were not his best friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You know that. Now, was this addressed particularly to those who were mixed marriages, as you said? You said you were half a Muslim, and you said that you have a Serbian wife, but that does not make you half a Muslim. Is one of your parents a Serb? Not only your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: None of my parents are Serbs. I'm a Muslim, but I do not have strong feelings about it. We are Europeans, and I don't think that there are great differences between people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm not asking your opinion; I'm asking you the reason why you said you are half a Muslim. Because your wife is a Serb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Do you think this is the reason why Mr. Jelisic took the trouble to risk his life to save you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: I was in such great danger, my life was threatened, at risk. And Goran, as a very good acquaintance, helped me, and that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness DJ. I have a few questions I would like to ask. You said that you met Mr. Jelisic in school. After school, about how many times did you meet Mr. Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Bijelina was a small town. We would meet frequently. Most often we would sit in a cafe near his house, drink, and talk about girls and sports and topics like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of that when you were not abroad? I mean, you were not in Germany and you were not in Austria; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes, between -- between my absences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bijelina, as you say, is a small town. Did you know what Mr. Jelisic did for work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: For a while, he worked in a company in Novo Selo, (redacted). And as far as the rest of his career is concerned, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment, at that time when Mr. Jelisic helped you, do you know what he was doing? Do you know what kind of work he was doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not work at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did Mr. Jelisic help other people in the same way that he helped you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was those people's ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DJ
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are my questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness DJ. Your testimony is complete. The Tribunal thanks you for having answered Mr. Greaves' summons, Mr. Greaves who was Mr. Jelisic's Defence counsel. We're going to take a break, which will allow the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom. We will take a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we resume the hearing. Have the witness brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Presiding Judge speaking to you, sir. First, see if this is, in fact, your name on the document which is being shown to you. Don't state your name. Is that, in fact, your name and your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please take an oath now, and then after that, you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated now, Witness DK. Mr. Greaves must have explained to you how all of this is going to work. Do not be afraid. Speak without any fear. You are in front of Judges. Mr. Greaves will start by asking you some questions because you are a Defence witness, well, in favour of the accused who is sitting at your left, and then it will be the Prosecutor asking you questions, and finally the Judges will ask some questions too. Mr. Greaves, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DK, would you tell us, please, what is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: I'm a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And would you please tell us what your home town is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: I live in the town of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And were you living in Brcko in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was born on the territory of the town of Brcko and have lived in the centre of town since 1962.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to ask you, in particular, about May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would Your Honours give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting my learned colleague Mr. Greaves, but could Goran Jelisic leave for five minutes? He has some stomach pains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Goran Jelisic, the trial is going to continue, with your agreement and the agreement of the lawyers that it can go on without you for five minutes. All right, guards, take him out. But in any case, the hearings will stop at 6.00 today and will resume tomorrow morning. The guards can take Goran Jelisic out of the courtroom, and during that time we will continue. Please continue now, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DK, I was going to ask you about May 1992. Did you remain at home throughout the period of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: The whole month, and I'm there now. I never went anywhere, and I was there throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And this may seem like an obvious question, but did you become aware of the fighting that was taking place in your town in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Without telling us what the area of Brcko is in which you live, is that an area which is of mixed ethnicity in terms -- in May 1992, was it of mixed ethnicity, in terms of its residents, or was it of one single racial group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: (redacted) 4 (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: During May 1992, were any searches conducted by the police in your immediate area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Yes, and my house was ransacked too. The war began on the 1st of May, and on the 3rd, large-scale fighting broke out. On the 5th, the police came to search all the houses, looking for weapons, asking whether there were any people who were not there previously and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was Goran Jelisic amongst those police officers who conducted that search? Who conducted that search?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Prior to May 1992, had you ever met Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: No, I never met him until the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you met him on the 8th of May, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: On the 8th of May, he was walking around with a girl that is a relative of mine, and they were walking up my street, which is called (redacted) (redacted). And as that particular girl -- I'm her uncle, that is -- asked me whether they could stop for a cup of coffee, I said they could. I didn't know who Goran was. I just saw a young man of medium height. They were more or less the same age, and they were dating for a day or two, perhaps, before that, but I saw him for the first time on May the 8th. He was in my yard. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Just pause there. When you first saw him, was he in civilian clothing, or police uniform or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: No, he was wearing a police uniform of an olive-green colour. He had no cap on his head. He had a pistol on his -- and he had a baton. He didn't have a cap. He had no rank of any kind, and the pistol was attached to his belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The relative of yours with whom he was going out, did she also live nearby?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did the girl and Goran Jelisic ever come to your house during May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to get to know Goran Jelisic during those meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: I asked the boy -- he's a boy for me because he's young -- where he was from, and he said he was from Bijelina, and he said his name was Goran Jelisic. So I asked him what Milorad and Borka Jelisic were to him, (redacted), and he said "That is my uncle and aunt." Borka is a teacher, and his uncle is a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In May 1992, were you able to see Goran Jelisic with other people who lived in your area and the way in which he approached them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Goran used to walk alone mostly, and he went with this relative of mine to Bijelina. He took her home, and he would come to my place in the afternoon for a cup of coffee. And this was between the 8th and 10th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If you can just help me, please, did you see him with any of your neighbours and the way in which he spoke and addressed them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Yes. He would come up to my neighbours'. 24 (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: (redacted), and he would talk to all of them, but I didn't notice anything bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If I can ask you this, was his conduct towards them what you would describe as proper conduct, or did he insult them in any way, make reference to their racial background or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: No, he did not. On the contrary, my neighbour Mustafa said that he offered to do anything for him if he needed this, any food or clothing or footwear. And Esad said that too. He said to me, "Uncle [redacted], do you need anything?" And I said I didn't need a thing, because in 1992, at the beginning of the year, we had everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you hear any complaint from anybody in your neighbourhood about his conduct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: During that time and my meetings with Goran, nobody had any complaints to make in all the three streets which surrounded my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you spoke with him, did he talk at any stage of the work that he was doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Yes; that is to say, I asked him. I said I saw that he was a policeman, and I knew that the army had come from Bijelina and that they had set up a front, and he said that he was a reserve policeman. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he give you any detail of what his job entailed, what his job involved doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Well, the police -- well, many armies walked about; there was fighting going on. And I didn't even dare ask him any details, because I'm an elderly citizen, I'm a pensioner, and I was just interested in my own family and my own neighbourhood. And what the police and army did, I didn't even dare ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did there come a time in May 1992 after which you stopped seeing Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: When I stopped seeing Goran was when I stopped seeing him at all, and I heard nothing of him later on. This was between the 10th and 11th. He came to me at 3.30 in the afternoon, but it wasn't the Goran Jelisic that I had first met. He was exhausted, he was nervous, he wasn't in a good mood. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. Just describe his demeanour to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK
utterances.text: Well, he came, and as usual, I offered him some coffee. I have good plum brandy, too, and I have my own, but he never wanted any plum brandy. When I gave him a cup of coffee, my relative, Marija, would come from across the road, and I would ask him, "What's the matter, Goran?" Because he looked quite different. And he said, "Well, it's bad, Uncle [redacted]." And I said, "Well, what's bad, Goran? Can you tell me?" And he said, "Well, the authorities in Brcko are making me do some bad business, dirty business." And I said, "Well, Goran, don't do that. Leave, flee."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two things: First, this is not foreshadowed in the summary. Second, there is objection in principle of any second-hand account of what Jelisic was doing when it's open to him to give evidence himself. These are matters merely in relation to character and mitigation, and what we are hearing now is second-hand, something that could come from the defendant himself. And there is no grounds for admitting it in this form. We object to this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the summary, yes, it was short, and that's true, Mr. Nice, but for the time being we have the summary that we have. The one from the Defence is very concise. Sometimes yours did not always match what was going on. I think that they have to be taken as working instruments. As regards the questions, for the time being, I really cannot agree with what you said secondly, that is, with your objection. I think that the hearsay testimony, which, as you know, in various systems is accepted, more or less. Each party in this Tribunal has been able to deal with the issue of hearsay, including the Prosecution. Therefore, for the time being, I think that the witness is justified in saying, in favour of the accused, that he had received his niece and that apparently she had a relatively close relationship with Jelisic; and I think that for the time being, at least, we can continue with that question. In any case, I would suggest that perhaps, since it's now 6.00, that we should resume tomorrow morning at 10.00. Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 6.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of November, 1999, at 10.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
